_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्येत्यत्र हेतुमाह इन्द्रियाणामिति
he gives the reason for ‘the undisciplined has no understanding’ with ‘of the senses’
इन्द्रियाणामवशीकृतानां स्वैरं विषयेषु चरतां मध्ये यदेवैकमिन्द्रियं मनोऽनुविधीयतेऽवशीकृतं सदिन्द्रियेण सह गच्छति
among uncontrolled senses freely moving among objects, whichever single sense the mind follows, itself uncontrolled, the mind goes together with that sense
तदेवैकमिन्द्रियमस्य मनसः पुरुषस्य वा प्रज्ञां हरति विषयविक्षिप्तां करोति
that one sense alone carries away the wisdom of the mind, or of the person, making it distracted by objects
किमुत वक्तव्यं बहूनि प्रज्ञां हरन्तीति
what need is there to say that many senses carry it away?
यथा प्रमत्तस्य कर्णधारस्य नावं वायुः समुद्रे सर्वतः परिभ्रामयति तद्वत्
just as wind drives in every direction on the ocean the boat of a heedless helmsman, so it is
इन्द्रियसंयमस्य स्थितप्रज्ञत्वसाधनत्वलक्षणत्वं प्रोक्तमुपसंहरति यस्मादिति
he concludes what has been stated, that restraint of the senses is both a means to and a characteristic of steady wisdom, with ‘therefore’
प्रतिष्ठिता भवतीत्यर्थः
it becomes established; this is the meaning
लक्षणत्वोपसंहारे तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ज्ञातव्येत्यर्थः
in concluding its status as a characteristic, his wisdom is to be known as established; this is the meaning
महाबाहो इति संबोधनं वैरिनिग्रहसमर्थस्य तवात्रापि सामर्थ्यं भवेदिति सूचयति
the address ‘O mighty-armed’ indicates that you who are capable of restraining enemies should be capable here also
ननु च कश्चिदपि प्रसुप्त इव दर्शनादिव्यापारशून्यः सर्वात्मना निगृहीतेन्द्रियो लोके न दृश्यते अतोऽसंभावितमिदं लक्षणमित्याशङ्क्याह या निशेति

objection: no one is seen in the world with senses restrained in every way, devoid of seeing and other activities as if asleep; therefore this characteristic seems impossible; anticipating this he says ‘what is night’
सर्वेषां भूतानां या निशा निशेव निशा आत्मनिष्ठा आत्माज्ञानध्वान्तावृतमतीनां तस्यां दर्शनादिव्यवहाराभावात्

that which is night for all beings is establishment in the Self, like night because for those whose minds are covered by the darkness of ignorance of the Self there is no activity such as seeing in it
तस्यामात्मनिष्ठायां संयमी निगृहीतेन्द्रियो जागर्ति प्रबुध्यते
in that establishment in the Self, the restrained one whose senses are controlled is awake, awakened
यस्यां तु विषयबुद्ध्या भूतानि जाग्रति प्रबुद्ध्यन्ते सा आत्मतत्त्वं पश्यतो मुनेर्निशा
but that in which beings are awake through cognition of objects is night for the sage who sees the truth of the Self
तस्यां दर्शनादिव्यापारस्तस्य नास्तीत्यर्थः
in that state he has no activity of seeing objects and the like; this is the meaning
एतदुक्तं भवति यथा दिवान्धानामुलूकादीनां रात्रावेव दर्शनं न तु दिवसे
this is what is said: just as creatures blind by day, such as owls, see only at night and not by day
एवं ब्रह्मज्ञस्योन्मीलिताक्षस्यापि ब्रह्मण्येव दृष्टिर्नतु विषयेषु
so even with eyes open, the knower of Brahman sees Brahman alone and not sense objects
अतो नासंभावितमिदं लक्षणमिति
therefore this characteristic is not impossible
ननु विषयेषु दृष्ट्यभावे कथमसौ तान्भुङ्क्त इत्यपेक्षायामाह आपूर्यमाणमिति
objection: if he has no vision directed toward objects, how does he experience them? in answer he says ‘being filled’
नानानदीभिरापूर्यमाणमपि अचलप्रतिष्ठमनतिक्रान्तमर्यादमेव समुद्रं पुनरप्यन्या आपो यथा प्रविशन्ति
just as other waters continually enter the ocean which, though being filled by many rivers, remains firmly established and does not cross its boundary
तथा कामा विषया यं मुनिमन्तर्दृष्टिं भोगैरविक्रियमाणमेव प्रारब्धकर्मभिराक्षिप्ताः सन्तः प्रविशन्ति
so objects of desire, impelled by prārabdha karma, enter the inward-looking sage without changing him through their enjoyments
स शान्तिं कैवल्यं प्राप्नोति नतु कामकामी भोगकामनाशीलः
he attains peace, liberation, not one who desires desires and habitually longs for enjoyment
यस्मादेवं तस्मात् विहायेति
because this is so, therefore with ‘abandoning’
प्राप्तान्कामान्विहाय त्यक्त्वोपेक्ष्य अप्राप्तेषु च निःस्पृहः
abandoning, relinquishing, disregarding desires that have been obtained and without longing for those not obtained
यतो निरहंकारः अतएव तद्भोगसाधनेषु निर्ममः सन्
being free from ego, and therefore without possessiveness regarding the means of enjoying them
अन्तर्दृष्टिर्भूत्वा यश्चरति प्रारब्धवशेन भोगान्भुङ्क्ते यत्र क्वापि गच्छति वा
one who moves about with inward vision, experiencing enjoyments under the force of prārabdha or going wherever he may
स शान्तिमाप्नोति
he attains peace
उक्तां ज्ञाननिष्ठां स्तुवन्नुपसंहरति एषेति
praising the steadfastness in knowledge just described, he concludes with ‘this’
ब्राह्मीस्थितिर्ब्रह्मज्ञाननिष्ठा एषा एवंविधा
this Brahmic state is steadfastness in knowledge of Brahman of the kind just described
एनां परमेश्वराराधनेन शुद्धान्तःकरणः पुमान् प्राप्य न विमुह्यति पुनः संसारमोहं न प्राप्नोति
a person whose inner instrument has been purified through worship of the Supreme Lord, attaining this, is not again deluded and does not again fall into the delusion of saṃsāra
यतः अन्तकाले मृत्युसमयेऽप्यस्यां क्षणमात्रमपि स्थित्वा ब्रह्मणि निर्वाणं लयमृच्छति प्राप्नोति
because even at the final moment, the time of death, remaining in it for only an instant, he attains nirvāṇa, dissolution in Brahman
किं पुनर्वक्तव्यं बाल्यमारभ्य स्थित्वा प्राप्नोतीति
what need is there to say that one established in it from childhood attains it?
